G1_rules.note: Not a hardware designer's review. 227 rules kept (45 rejected, 7 merged). 19 spec-lint gaps answered as spec section 10 decisions D-001..D-022 (documents only; where they are silent or disagree, only the common part or a bound is checked). 8 open questions answered on delegation: run set = all four parameter combinations; counting convention for D-018 at the ports; status-type interrupts, pings and sender encoding-error timing out of scope. Where a kept rule conflicts with a decision, the decision limits the check: GP-T5.11-02/GP-T5.12-02 (MASKED_OE read bits 31:16) by D-002, CP-T1.8.4-05 (INTR_STATE not qualified by INTR_ENABLE) by D-004. Open for the G4 reviewer: D-002, D-004.

G2_contract.note: Not a hardware designer's review. 38 checks (13 assertions, 25 tests) over 188 rules; 80 rules not verifiable by simulation (mostly standard text outside this IP, status-type interrupts, pings, obligations of the host). Checks follow D-001..D-022: bounds instead of exact cycles where the documents are silent (filter D-007, latencies D-018); MASKED_OE read bits 31:16 unchecked (D-002); INTR_STATE checked only where both readings of D-004 agree. Run set: base (2 seeds), sync_off, straps_off, min.

G3_verif_sources.note: Not a hardware designer's review. Re-approved after fix-verif from the formal counterexample of CHK-003: a request with i_a_intg_flip=1 counts as an alert cause from i_a_valid=1, not only from its A handshake (INT-INTG-002, INT-TL-003, D-017 gives only an upper bound). Traffic with i_a_intg_flip=0 is still never a cause. Candidate passes 26/26 tests and 13/13 assertions in all 5 runs.
